item.title: Version 1.11.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.11.0

This update lets an AI assistant such as Claude use ScoreSort for you (in beta), adds sorting parts into section folders, and makes scans of double pages much easier to split.

✨ General Improvements

  • (Beta) Ask an AI assistant to do the job, and it can use ScoreSort. Tell an AI like Claude "split this scan into parts, name them and number them in score order" and it can now work ScoreSort for you. It looks at the pages to read the part names, then uses ScoreSort's own splitting, double-page scan cutting, score-order renaming, combining with your presets, stamping, and sorting parts into section folders, so the files come out exactly as they would from the app. It works as a command-line tool for AI tools with a terminal, and as an "MCP server" for chat apps such as the Claude desktop app. It can also combine a folder of parts for one of your ensemble presets and sort out who plays what — spotting players with no part (say, two bass guitars) and giving them the closest one (the tuba part), spreading percussion across the percussion parts, and asking you before it hands anyone a part in the wrong key. Share the folders you keep parts and scans in, and you can just say "the Holst scan" — your assistant sees nothing else on your Mac; for anything else, paste a file's path (⌥⌘C in Finder). It never replaces a file unless told to, and it can show what it's about to do first. To set it up, open Settings ▸ AI Assistants and click Connect to Claude (or Install Command for AI tools that work in a terminal).
  • Page previews in the Split and Rotate tabs are quicker to render.

🏷️ Rename Files

  • Sort parts into section subfolders. There is a new Sort into folders menu — beside the Rename button in the Renamer, and on the score-order step when splitting or bulk renaming. This lets ScoreSort put each part in a folder for its section — Woodwind, Brass, Percussion and Strings for a concert band (piano and string bass go with the brass), or Saxophones, Trumpets, Trombones and Rhythm for a jazz band — or for its instrument (Flute, Clarinet, Alto Saxophone…). The score and any part ScoreSort doesn't recognise stays at the top. Split several pieces into the same folder and their parts collect in the same section folders. In the Renamer, parts that are already numbered are simply moved into their folders. If ScoreSort puts a part in the wrong folder (say, a Bass part you'd rather keep with the strings), drag it onto another folder or right-click it; you can also make a new folder or keep a part at the top.
  • "Renumber prefixed files" stays as you set it. Ticked once, it stays ticked for every folder you drop — including each folder in a batch — until you quit ScoreSort, instead of unticking itself for each new folder.

🔗 Combine PDFs

  • Moving files after adding them no longer breaks Combine. ScoreSort now keeps track of each file you add, so if you move or rename it in Finder before making the PDF, it still finds it — and the list and table of contents pick up the new name. (A file you've moved to the Trash counts as gone.)

✂️ Split PDF

  • Scans of double pages are much easier to split. The A3 splitter has grown into Split Double Pages, built for overhead and book scanners. Every scan is shown in one window: two-page scans are cut at the gap between the pages — wherever it actually is, not just down the middle — single pages are left whole, and black scanner background or empty facing pages are set aside to skip. Drag a cut line to move it, switch any scan between one page and two, or click a page to skip or keep it. Skipped pages stay in Step 1, greyed out, so nothing is lost. It's offered when you open such a scan, or from Fix Scan ▸ Split Double Pages…. For scans of identical sheets, like A3 from a flatbed scanner, every page gets the same cut — down the middle, or wherever you drag any one of them — so you can just press Return and go.
  • ScoreSort now asks what to do with a PDF's bookmarks — and can name the files from them. When you open a PDF that already has bookmarks, a sheet shows the names its bookmarks would give the files. Choose Split & Name Files to split at the bookmarks and use their titles as the file names (either "Piece - Flute 1" or just the bookmark title on its own), Split Only to keep the split points and name the files yourself, or Ignore Bookmarks to start from scratch. Before, the splits appeared without warning and the titles were only used for PDFs made by ScoreSort's own Combine tab.

🔖 Stamp

  • Moving files after adding them no longer breaks stamping. If you move or rename a queued file in Finder, the Stamp tab still finds it — “Replace original files” stamps it where it is now, and a new name carries through to “Save as new files” unless you’ve typed your own. If a file can’t be stamped, ScoreSort now says why.

🐞 Fixed

  • Typing a number for a file in the Renamer works. When you double-click a file to give it a number, the number you type is now used.
  • No more two files with the same number. Dropping in a folder where some parts are already numbered and some aren't used to number the new ones from 01 again, clashing with the old ones. The Renamer now renumbers the whole folder in that case (ticking "Renumber prefixed files" for you and saying so); untick it if you really want only the new files numbered.
  • "Renumber prefixed files" puts parts of the same instrument in order. A folder numbered with Trombone 3 before Trombone 2 used to keep that order ("already correct"); renumbering now fixes it, and "Trumpet 2" comes after "Trumpet 1".
  • A single part can go through the splitter once its pages have been cut or reordered. If you split a part scanned as A3 sheets into A4 pages (or fixed its booklet order, or swapped pages) and it's still one file, you can now carry on through naming and saving — before, both steps insisted on at least two files or a skipped page, even though the result was a new PDF.
  • The little page map beside each page preview when naming parts (Split and Bulk Rename) now marks exactly what you can see. Its rectangle used to be about three times taller than the area actually shown, and you couldn't pan all the way to the bottom of a page.
  • After splitting a scan, Delete skips one page again, not the whole file, as intended — so removing a stray blank page doesn't take the rest of the part with it.
  • Combine says what went wrong instead of “Failed to create PDF”. If a file in the list has been deleted or can’t be read since you added it, ScoreSort now names it and says why, rather than giving a one-line error — or, if only some files were affected, quietly leaving those parts out of the PDF. Problems saving to a folder (such as a read-only shared drive) are explained too.
  • Combined PDFs keep their table of contents on macOS 27. Booklets, and any combined PDF with a stamp on it, were being saved without their bookmarks, so there was no list of parts in Preview's sidebar and the Split tab couldn't find the part boundaries by itself. The bookmarks are saved again, for Create PDF and Open in Preview.

item.title: Version 1.10.1
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.10.1

A follow-up to 1.10.0 with a few booklet and preset improvements.

🔗 Combine PDFs

  • Single-sided booklets. When every part fits on one side of a sheet — a folder of two-page parts, say — the output no longer carries a blank back for each one.
  • Bass guitar matches the bass part. A preset entry for Bass Guitar now finds a String Bass, Double Bass or Contrabass file, and the other way round — the player reads whichever one is in the folder.
  • Presets divide copies between split parts. If your preset says Trumpet: 7 but the music comes as separate 1st and 2nd trumpet files, applying it used to put 7 on each. It now shares the count out (4 and 3), and tints those rows blue so you can see the app made the call and adjust it.

🐞 Fixed

  • The combined PDF's contents list lands on the right part. Clicking a name in Preview's sidebar now jumps to the top of the page, as you'd expect.

item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.10.0

This update contains a lot of improvements to the Combine tab, and a few bug fixes in the rest of the app.

🔗 Combine — major new feature: Booklets!

  • Booklets. Switch the output menu at the bottom left from Single pages to Booklet, and every part is laid out as its own fold-and-staple booklet — the whole folder in one print job, instead of one document at a time. Full size prints multiple A4 parts onto A3 paper. (You can also print in A5 onto an A4 booklet if you want to.) Each copy of a part becomes its own booklet, and short parts are padded out to a whole folded sheet automatically. Two-page parts are laid out flat — both pages side by side on one sheet — so you can open them on the stand and never turn a page mid-piece.
  • Choose where the page turns fall. When creating a booklet, you can specify how to arrange the pages for sensible page turns. When in booklet mode, try the Page Turns (⌘T) button to view each part and specify where you want to place your page breaks.
  • Booklet page scale. Published music rarely matches A4 exactly, so a Scale box beside the output menu sizes each page within its half of the sheet — above 100% to fill more of the page, below it for more space around the music.
  • Two-sided printing setup. macOS doesn't let an app choose your two-sided setting, and printers differ in which edge they turn the paper on. Set Up Two-Sided Printing… in the output menu prints one numbered test sheet: fold it, say whether the pages came out the right way up, and ScoreSort sets the rest for you, remembered for each printer you use.
  • Print without saving first. A new Print… button (⌘P) sends the combined PDF straight to the print dialog in one step, alongside Create PDF and Open in Preview.

🔗 Combine — other improvements

  • Press Space to look at a file in the list. Quick Look opens on the file you've got selected, just like in Finder — arrow keys move to the next part, Space or Escape closes it again.
  • The Presets button now looks like a button, and stays visibly switched on while the presets panel is open.

🐞 Fixed

  • Renamer: switching ensemble works every time. After the first change, picking a different ensemble moved the buttons but carried on matching against the previous ensemble's instruments — so on Orchestra, an Oboe or Violin part could come up "not recognised" because it was still checking the Jazz Band list.
  • Split: keyboard navigation works again. Clicking an output file left the arrow keys unable to page through the PDF, and in Step 2 Tab jumped to a preview arrow instead of the next instrument name. Sorry!
  • ⌘W now closes the window as you'd hope — it previously did nothing.
  • One View menu instead of two. The menu bar had two menus both called View; the tab shortcuts now live in the standard one alongside Full Screen.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.9.0

✨ New: the Stamp tool

  • Add a small text overlay to your parts — "Example School Band", "Property of the Music Dept" — the way you'd use a rubber stamp. Design and save any number of stamps (⌘5), one per school or ensemble.
  • Set the text and style — font, size, colour, and bold or italic on just the words you choose — plus an optional box around it.
  • Put it anywhere on the page: click one of nine quick positions, or drag the stamp around on a live preview of your own part.
  • Type {date} or {year} for a copy date, filled in when the stamp is applied — day-first by default.
  • Stamp files you already have (PDFs and images), a folder at a time, replacing the originals or saving copies under names you type.
  • Stamps are burned into the page, so they print everywhere and can't be deleted out of the PDF.

🔗 Combine

  • New Stamp button in the toolbar — stamp the combined PDF as it's created, on every page or just the first page of each part.
  • Presets can carry a stamp: applying your ensemble's preset arms its stamp.
  • Fixed: clicking a file now selects just that file (it used to behave as though ⌘ was held), and ⌫ removes selected files again.

✂️ Split

  • New Stamp button in Step 1, with the stamp shown on the preview of pages that will get one.
  • More instruments in the naming suggestions (alto/bass flute, oboe d'amore, cor anglais, clarinet in B♭ and A, drum kit, vibraphone, mallet percussion, and a combined "Trombone Baritone Bassoon" part), with spelling variants treated as one instrument.
  • A tidier Step 1 toolbar and consistent headings across all three steps.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.8.0

✨ General

  • Many more keyboard shortcuts! ⌘O/⌘S/⇧⌘P/⌘⌫/⌘R now do what you might expect them to. In the combiner, ⇧⌘P pushes you out to Preview, ready to print with ⌘P. You can also always open the folder you're working in with ⇧⌘F. See the Help menu for a full Keyboard Shortcuts reference.
  • Redesigned menu bar — proper File / View / per-tab Actions menus now cover much more of the app's functionality.
  • Many more significant but invisible changes under the hood.

✂️ Split

  • Jazz naming suggestions overhauled.
  • Return / Escape to move between steps with the keyboard.
  • It's now easier to promote unmatched files in Step 3 using the arrow keys.

🔗 Combine

  • Preset sidebar now live-syncs with Preferences.
  • Much smarter preset matching between the side panel and the files you've dragged in (abbreviations/aliases are now understood, clef-precise euphonium, "Clarinet" ≠ "Bass Clarinet").
  • Collate groups get their own colour, distinct from your selection colour.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.7.0

✨ General improvements

  • Drop a new file onto the “Done” screen to start the next job immediately, without clicking Start Over (Rename, Bulk Rename, and Split).

🏷️ Rename Files

  • Batch renaming. Rename multiple folders of pieces at once — drag in a parent folder of nested folders, or several folders together, and the app walks you through them one after another.
  • You can now rename image scans (e.g. JPGs) as well as PDFs.

🔗 Combine PDFs

  • Drag to reorder files. Collate groups move as a unit, and you can drop a file onto a group to add it in.

✂️ Split PDF

  • Undo/redo while splitting. ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z undo and redo split-point, skip, and re-stride edits in Step 1.
  • Drag to pan the part preview in the naming step (the page strip or its minimap), not just the arrow buttons.
  • Much smarter instrument-name suggestions, now driven by the selected ensemble (Wind Band / Jazz Band / Orchestra): suggestions follow that ensemble’s real score order (e.g. Horn follows Trumpet in a band), use ensemble-aware part counts, prefer full instrument names, and handle the clarinet family and baritone/euphonium better.
  • Duplicate-name warning when two files would get the same name; saving is blocked if they’d truly collide.
  • General improvements to the score-order prefix screen.

🐞 Fixed

  • Keyboard shortcuts are now strictly limited to the current tab.
  • The part-name preview no longer clips the instrument name at the top of the page.
  • Dragging a new PDF onto the splitter’s “Done” screen no longer leaves a blank Step 1 preview.

item.title: Version 1.6.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.6.0

New

  • Splitter — move the original to Trash. A new checkbox on Step 2 cleans up the source PDF after your split files are saved. Off by default, remembered between uses, and recoverable (it goes to the Trash).
  • Splitter — A3 page preview. The "which half comes first?" dialog now shows a preview of your actual page behind the left/right selector.

Improved

  • Easier-to-hit “Clear” buttons in every tool.

Fixed

  • The app no longer quits from the update dialog at launch.
  • No “check for updates automatically?” prompt on the very first launch.

item.title: Version 1.5.2
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.5.2

Reliability fix: automatic updates now install correctly. (Earlier versions couldn't complete an in-app update — please update manually this once, and future updates will be automatic.)

item.title: Version 1.5.1
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.5.1

A small polish update:

  • Expanded the Welcome Tour — clearer guidance for combining (images, blank pages, table of contents) and splitting, including A3 sheet splitting and booklet reordering.
  • Tidied the default window size and minor UI refinements.
